newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman Energy makes bid for Wascana Energy.
newsitem.headline: Talisman Energy makes bid for Wascana Energy.

text.p: Talisman Energy Inc. said on Wednesday it planned to make a cash and stock takeover offer for Regina, Saskatchewan-based Wascana Energy Inc.

In an much-anticipated announcement, Talisman of Calgary said it would offer C$18.50 ($13.69) cash or 0.41 of one of its shares for each share of Wascana, a former Saskatchewan government-owned oil company.

Talisman said the total value of the deal would be C$1.7 billion ($1.3 billion), based on 40 percent of Wascana shares being sold for cash and the rest being swapped for Talisman stock. The offer also includes the assumption of about C$200 million ($148 million) in long-term debt.

"Talisman has the track record, the financial strength and the operating experience to make these assets grow," Talisman Chief Executive Jim Buckee said in a statement. "Wascana and Talisman combined will provide an outstanding platform for growth both in Canada and internationally and our balance sheet remains strong."

Long a rumored suitor for Wascana -- a company known largely for heavy oil production in Saskatchewan -- Talisman said the deal would double its landholdings in western Canada and increase its 1997 oil and gas production by 30 percent to 175,000 barrels per day of oil and 826 million cubic feet per day of natural gas.

Talisman, which had 10.3 percent of Wascana shares locked into its offer, said that if the deal was successful, it would make the Saskatchewan firm a wholly owned subsidiary and keep its head office in Regina, as is spelled out in provincial legislation.
